pr.title: [Coverage][MCDC] Group mcdc tests and fix panic when generating mcdc code for inlined expressions.
pr.description:
### Changes

1. Group all mcdc tests to one directory.
2. Since mcdc instruments different mappings for boolean expressions with normal branch coverage as #125766 introduces, it would be better also trace branch coverage results in mcdc tests.
3. So far rustc does not call `CoverageInfoBuilderMethods::init_coverage` for inlined functions. As a result, it could panic if it tries to instrument mcdc statements for inlined functions due to uninitialized cond bitmaps. We can reproduce this issue by current nightly rustc and [the test](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/127234/files#diff-c81af6bf4869aa42f5c7334e3e86344475de362f673f54ce439ec75fcb5ac3e5) with flag `--release`. This patch fixes it.
pr.author: ZhuUx

processing.reason: The historical defect is a compiler-pass enablement bug, not a semantics-changing MIR rewrite. PR #127234 only makes `Inline::is_enabled` return false when MCDC coverage is active; the inlined vs non-inlined Rust program still computes the same boolean value (`a && b`). The historical failure is that coverage instrumentation instruments inlined MIR without `init_coverage`, using uninitialized condition bitmaps and potentially panicking at compile/instrumentation time. That is not observable as a different defined runtime value for any concrete input, so it cannot be encoded by two ordinary Rust functions with identical signatures that both pass Miri and return different values. Emulating it by deliberately reading uninitialized bitmap state or by adding unrelated return-value differences would manufacture semantics absent from the PR and would not validate the historical transformation. The regression test's `.coverage`/`.cov-map` difference is instrumentation metadata, not a source-level value change, and the supplied frozen analysis explicitly warns that a coverage-count mismatch is not the failure to model.

analysis.summary: The MIR `Inline` pass must be disabled while MCDC coverage instrumentation is enabled. Historically, inlining MIR under MCDC caused coverage instrumentation to generate MCDC statements for inlined expressions even though `init_coverage` had not been called for the inlined function, leading to uninitialized condition bitmaps and a possible panic. This is a source-backed bug fix, not an optimization; the supplied patch only adds an MCDC guard to `Inline::is_enabled` and adds regression coverage. No compiler was built or executed for this knowledge extraction.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the fix, `Inline::is_enabled` did not check whether MCDC coverage was active; it first honored an explicit `-Zinline-mir` override, otherwise used the normal inlining decision. Thus the MIR inliner could run while `sess.instrument_coverage_mcdc()` was true.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was: under MCDC coverage instrumentation, allow the `Inline` pass to inline a function containing boolean/MCDC expressions into its caller. Coverage instrumentation then encountered inlined MIR for which `CoverageInfoBuilderMethods::init_coverage` had not been called, so it attempted to instrument MCDC statements using uninitialized condition bitmaps and could panic. The fix does not change MCDC generation itself; it prevents this inlining transformation when MCDC is enabled.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with MCDC coverage enabled, containing a function marked or selected for inlining whose body has boolean expressions that MCDC instruments, especially `a && b` returned from an `#[inline(always)]` function and called with several truth-value combinations. The historical failure is associated with optimized builds and MIR inlining; the added regression uses `-Zcoverage-options=mcdc -Copt-level=z -Cllvm-args=--inline-threshold=0` and `--show-branches=count --show-mcdc`. It is specifically MCDC coverage, not merely normal branch coverage.
analysis.trigger: The `Inline` MIR pass runs while `-Zcoverage-options=mcdc` / `sess.instrument_coverage_mcdc()` is enabled, and a call to a function containing MCDC-instrumented boolean expressions is inlined.
preconditions: MCDC coverage instrumentation is enabled via `sess.instrument_coverage_mcdc()`.
The `Inline` MIR pass is otherwise eligible to run; the explicit `-Zinline-mir` override must not bypass the MCDC guard.
The candidate callee contains boolean expression(s) for which MCDC statements are generated, such as `a && b`.
The historical compiler does not call `CoverageInfoBuilderMethods::init_coverage` for inlined functions.
pitfalls: Do not attribute this to `ForceInline`; the patch modifies `impl<'tcx> MirPass<'tcx> for Inline`, not a force-inline pass.
Do not generalize the guard to all coverage modes: the FIXME and check are specifically about Modified Condition/Decision Coverage.
Do not let the later `-Zinline-mir` override re-enable inlining after the MCDC check; the new check is placed before the unstable-option override and returns `false` immediately.
Do not confuse MIR inlining with LLVM inlining; `-Cllvm-args=--inline-threshold=0` in the regression helps isolate behavior while `#[inline(always)]` and MIR inlining remain relevant.
The failure is not merely a coverage-count mismatch: source text says uninitialized cond bitmaps can cause a panic when instrumenting MCDC statements for inlined functions.
A retained test filename or old comment does not itself prove pass behavior; compare the actual MIR/coverage-map effects.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct a focused compile/coverage regression: use an `#[inline(always)]` function whose body is a MCDC decision such as `a && b`, call it with `(true,false)`, `(false,true)`, and `(true,true)`, and compile with `-Zcoverage-options=mcdc -Copt-level=z -Cllvm-args=--inline-threshold=0`; check coverage with `--show-branches=count --show-mcdc`. Compare the same program with the MIR `Inline` transformation enabled under MCDC versus the corrected behavior where `Inline::is_enabled` returns false under MCDC. The important invariant is that compiling the MCDC-inlined case must not panic from uninitialized condition bitmaps, and the expected MCDC decision mappings should be represented in the `.cov-map`/`.coverage` regression outputs. The patch's added `tests/coverage/mcdc/inlined_expressions.rs` plus `.cov-map` and `.coverage` files provide the historical regression shape. Also retain coverage of non-inlined MCDC decisions and ordinary branch counts.
evidence: // FIXME(#127234): Coverage instrumentation currently doesn't handle inlined
// MIR correctly when Modified Condition/Decision Coverage is enabled.
So far rustc does not call `CoverageInfoBuilderMethods::init_coverage` for inlined functions.
As a result, it could panic if it tries to instrument mcdc statements for inlined functions due to uninitialized cond bitmaps.
